facts.text: Delegated Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions allow the application to read files and sites accessible to the signed-in user, constrained by the user's own authorization.

Administrator consent to delegated permissions does not grant the application an administrator role or application-only access; administrator consent can approve delegated permissions but does not imply elevated roles for the app.
Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps; consent does not automatically enable actions or connect accounts, and existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply.

Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, reviewing all permission requests centrally, and verifying the publisher and requested permissions before tenant-wide consent.
Review delegated versus application permissions explicitly, as they have different impacts; delegated permissions act on behalf of a user, while application permissions act as the app without a user.

recommendations: Review the specific delegated permissions requested and confirm they align with the business need and user roles before granting consent.
Implement an administrator approval workflow for permission requests to ensure centralized review and verification of publisher identity and permission scope.
Restrict user consent to verified publishers and selected permissions to reduce risk of excessive access.
Ensure service desk staff verify that delegated permissions are appropriate for the user's role and do not assume administrator consent grants elevated roles to the app.
Monitor granted permissions and review existing app consents regularly to detect any excessive or unexplained permissions.
unknowns: Whether the requested permissions have been reviewed and authorized by an administrator is unknown.
The exact process and controls implemented by the service desk for permission review and consent are unknown.
Whether the Personal plan supports all required controls or monitoring capabilities is unknown.
risks: Granting delegated Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions allows the app to read all files and sites accessible to the user, potentially exposing confidential or personal data if the user has broad access.
Administrator consent without proper review could lead to excessive permissions being granted, increasing data exposure risk.
If the service desk does not verify permission appropriateness, users might consent to permissions beyond their role, leading to unauthorized data access.

evidence.text: Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps, potentially performed by different administrators. Consent does not automatically connect individual accounts or enable actions. Existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply. Sites.Selected is not supported for live SharePoint search; supported ChatGPT site-collection restrictions are a separate mechanism.

evidence.text:
Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, with other requests reviewed centrally. An administrator approval workflow can support this process. Review existing apps and granted permissions; additional monitoring capabilities depend on licensing.

Before tenant-wide consent, verify the publisher and application identity, understand every requested permission, and match the request to the expected business functionality. Familiarity or widespread use is not sufficient justification. Do not grant permissions that are unexplained or appear excessive; obtain clarification from the publisher.

evidence.text: Where appropriate, consider user assignment restrictions for approved applications. Review delegated versus application permissions explicitly rather than assuming all consent requests have the same impact.

evidence.text:
Delegated access acts for an authenticated user. Both the application's granted scopes and the user's own authorization constrain access. Delegated Files.Read.All permits reading files accessible to that user.

Application permissions operate as the application without a signed-in user. The same permission name can have different implications: application Files.Read.All allows reading tenant files through Microsoft Graph. Application permissions and some privileged delegated scopes need administrator consent.

evidence.text: Consent authorizes specified permissions. An administrator can approve delegated permissions too, so the administrator's participation alone does not establish that the app has application-only access or an administrator role. Inspect the permission type and requested operations.

grounding_reason: All factual claims about delegated permissions, administrator consent, and the separation of consent and action enablement are directly supported by the cited evidence (MS-PERM-1, MS-PERM-2, OAI-ADMIN-2, OAI-LIVE-2). The risks and controls recommended align with Microsoft guidance on permission review and consent management (MS-REVIEW-1, MS-REVIEW-2). No invented capabilities, pricing, retention, or approval processes are asserted. Unknown fields are explicitly identified as unknown without guessing. No mixing of live/sync or subscription requirements occurs. The assessment correctly distinguishes delegated permissions from application permissions and clarifies that administrator consent does not grant an administrator role to ChatGPT. Therefore, the assessment is fully supported by the cited evidence.
